responseText: {"title":"Finding Faces in a Crowd","question":"What lets one face emerge from a crowded drawing?","introduction":"These twenty drawings share a single problem: too many marks, too many forms, too many possible faces. Some works announce their figures immediately; others bury them under crossing lines and competing shapes. Moving through the gallery, you are invited to notice what draws your eye to one face over another — outline, color, scale, or simply the gap between two marks.","closing":"Each drawing offers a different answer to the same question. Whether a face emerges depends on what the drawing withholds as much as what it shows.","chapters":[{"title":"One Face, Clearly There","introduction":"These works open the gallery with figures that hold their ground — readable faces that give the eye a place to land before the crowding begins.","stops":[{"slot":"W297","whyHere":"Eight black silhouettes press upward against a flat yellow field; their shared crossed marks make each head legible while the group reads as a single mass.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W144","whyHere":"A single hatted figure fills the frame; the contained head above and dissolving strokes below show one face holding while the rest of the image comes apart.","transitionFromPrevious":"From anonymous silhouettes to a named-feeling individual: the hat and concentric eye rings give this figure a specificity the crowd below lacked."},{"slot":"W102","whyHere":"A large face presses close to the picture edge, its layered eyes watchful; the lower blocks fragment beneath it, splitting the image into face and noise.","transitionFromPrevious":"The hatted figure was centered and stable; here the face crowds the frame edge, making legibility feel more pressured and less settled."},{"slot":"W055","whyHere":"A skull form holds center against a teal ground while color lines pull outward; the hollow eye sockets and clenched jaw keep the face readable despite the surrounding tangle.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous face was built from rings and fills; this one is structured by voids — the eye sockets are empty, making the skull legible through absence rather than mark."}]},{"title":"Faces Multiplying","introduction":"Recognizable figures begin to multiply here — mouths, eyes, and heads repeat across the surface until no single face commands the space alone.","stops":[{"slot":"W035","whyHere":"A skull contains a second face within it, while a smaller sun-face occupies the corner; three distinct presences occupy one image without merging.","transitionFromPrevious":"The skull in the previous work was singular and centered; here a second face nests inside the first, introducing the idea of faces containing faces."},{"slot":"W275","whyHere":"Three toothed mouths stack inside one bulging purple-red form, each paired with coiled eye marks — faces nested within a face, the surface layered and pressured.","transitionFromPrevious":"The nesting in the previous work was spatial — one skull around another; here the nesting is structural, three mouths built into a single form's body."},{"slot":"W269","whyHere":"A large circle on cobalt blue holds a heart, a flower, and a striped wedge that reads as a grin; competing interior forms make the circle itself feel face-like.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work nested faces explicitly; here the face is implied — a circle whose interior accumulates enough features to read as a head without declaring itself one."},{"slot":"W063","whyHere":"Dozens of small oval faces ring the border while larger open-mouthed figures crowd the center; the image is entirely populated, with no neutral ground remaining.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work held its forms inside one circle; here faces escape every boundary, lining the edges and filling the center simultaneously."},{"slot":"W086","whyHere":"A broad arched form anchors the center while a smaller snarling figure crowds the upper left; two figures at different scales pull against each other without resolving.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work distributed faces evenly across the surface; here scale difference creates hierarchy — one large form, one small intruder, neither yielding."}]},{"title":"The Crowd Turns Loud","introduction":"Color and mark-making intensify here. Mouths open, lines multiply, and the drawings become harder to read as any single scene.","stops":[{"slot":"W176","whyHere":"Four open-mouthed forms crowd an amber field, each built from looping spirals and jagged teeth; white lines move freely across all of them, refusing to settle into any one figure.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work held two figures in tension; here four faces press forward simultaneously, the amber ground pushing them all toward the viewer at once."},{"slot":"W223","whyHere":"Five spiky-ringed faces crowd a near-black ground; a lone pink flower and yellow spiral sit above the central figure as the only calm shapes in an otherwise agitated surface.","transitionFromPrevious":"The amber warmth of the previous work is replaced by near-black; the faces are now ringed by jagged lines rather than looping ones, sharpening the sense of alarm."},{"slot":"W185","whyHere":"Six oval heads rise in a row, mouths open, bodies dissolving into white streaks; the soft pink background circles pull against the density of the figures above them.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work scattered its faces across the field; here they line up in a row, introducing order — but the dissolving bodies undercut any sense of stability."},{"slot":"W239","whyHere":"Five round-headed figures are pressed forward by white outlines against loud color bands; two open mouths range from comic to unsettled, keeping the gathering's mood unresolved.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous row of heads dissolved downward into streaks; these figures are outlined and sticker-sharp, their edges holding even as the color bands behind them compete."},{"slot":"W204","whyHere":"Black rectangular masses and hot color zones pack the plane; a red-outlined face near the bottom — wide eyes, open mouth, arms spread — reads as exposed against the surrounding density.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work used white outlines to separate figures from ground; here no such separation exists — the face is caught inside the same density as everything around it."}]},{"title":"Figures Crossing, Outlines Shared","introduction":"These works push toward maximum density. Figures overlap until one form's edge becomes another's body, and looking becomes a process of finding, losing, and finding again.","stops":[{"slot":"W124","whyHere":"A seated central figure extends limbs outward while bared teeth recur at the margins; a floating white rectangle holds open a gap in the surrounding density.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work buried its face in color masses; here a figure has limbs and posture, but the repeated mouth fragments at the edges keep it from reading as singular."},{"slot":"W134","whyHere":"Three figures caught mid-action — arms raised, teeth out, dome swelling between them — share a black sky without any one commanding the space; spectacle and unease coexist.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work's figures were pressed flat by color; here depth is suggested by a black sky and spatial separation, yet the figures still compete rather than recede."},{"slot":"W045","whyHere":"A black mass holds center against an orange field while blue slashes cut across at angles; the white bar cluster reads as both noise and anchor in a composition that refuses to settle.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work distributed figures across a legible space; here the central form is ambiguous — mass rather than figure — and the crossing diagonals deny any stable reading."},{"slot":"W210","whyHere":"Several toothy heads overlap with raised limb-like forms; broad cyan passages open brief gaps, but one face's outline keeps becoming part of another's body.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work's ambiguity came from a single dominant mass; here multiple heads compete, and the cyan gaps are the only breathing room in the tangle."},{"slot":"W233","whyHere":"Heads and limb-like forms weave together in colored marks; the drawing alternates between recognizable characters and almost illegible crossings, making looking a repeated act of finding and losing.","transitionFromPrevious":"This work shares its figures and cyan passages with the previous one, but the marks are denser and the crossings more complete — legibility is harder won here."}]},{"title":"When the Lines Take Over","introduction":"The final works pull back from readable figures entirely, leaving the visitor to ask whether a face was ever there — or whether the marks themselves were always the subject.","stops":[{"slot":"W086","whyHere":"Revisited here as a transition: the arched central form and snarling corner figure now read as the last legible anchors before the compositions ahead dissolve further.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work made faces hard to hold; this one offers a brief return to two distinct forms — a pause before the final dissolution."},{"slot":"W102","whyHere":"The watchful layered eyes and fragmented lower blocks now read as a hinge: face above, abstraction below, the two zones pulling the image in opposite directions.","transitionFromPrevious":"The arched form gave the eye a clear shape to follow; here the face is present but the lower third has already broken into blocks, signaling the coming loss of figure."},{"slot":"W029","whyHere":"Yellow bands, a red spiral, and crossing lines fill the field without resolving into a face; the grey-green ground recedes behind marks that suggest a figure without confirming one.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work split face from abstraction vertically; here the split is gone — the whole surface is marks, and any face found is the viewer's own construction."},{"slot":"W275","whyHere":"Three nested toothed mouths inside one form return the gallery to its central question: are these faces, or marks that have accumulated enough features to be read as faces?","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work offered no clear face at all; this one presses three mouths forward insistently, demanding a decision the image itself refuses to make."},{"slot":"W297","whyHere":"The gallery closes where it opened: eight silhouettes under a yellow field, their crossed marks the minimum required for a face — proof that a crowd needs very little to be read as watching.","transitionFromPrevious":"The nested mouths were dense and pressured; these silhouettes are stripped to outline and two marks each, showing how little a drawing needs to hold a face in place."}]}]}
